_doc: NAMED CONFORMANCE GAPS. A place where busbar's bytes and a vendor's PUBLISHED schema disagree,
the disagreement has been read, and the owner has ruled that the bytes are right and the schema
is the thing that is incomplete. Every entry here turns ONE named violation on ONE named row
from FAIL into the rig's named-gap status (SKIP): still printed, still counted, still excluded
from the owed set, never a PASS. The validator is not touched — it still finds the violation, and
any violation on the same row that this file does not name still fails the row.
An entry is refused at load time unless it names an owner, a reason, the exact rule, a substring
of the violation's own detail, and the explicit list of ledger rows it covers. There are no
wildcards: a gap that could match a rule across a whole dialect is a bypass, not a gap.
An entry that names a row the run JUDGED and did not produce its violation on is STALE, and a
stale entry is RED (run.sh refuses before the verdict). A gap that has been fixed cannot sit here

gaps.why: The Anthropic streaming API DOCUMENTS a `ping` event and tells clients they may see one at any point in a message stream; the published schema's MessageStreamEvent union does not list it. Both statements are Anthropic's. Where the two disagree the wire the vendor's own clients are built to read wins, so busbar's Anthropic writer emits the ping when it composes a stream itself (the four cross-dialect egress lanes here); the same-dialect lane passes the upstream's bytes through and so never reaches this. Dropping the event to satisfy the union would make busbar's stream differ from the one Anthropic describes, which is the opposite of what this rig is for.

gaps.detail_contains: ServiceQuotaExceededException is not an error Converse/ConverseStream declare
gaps.why: `ServiceQuotaExceededException` is a real, documented Bedrock Runtime error type that the Converse and ConverseStream operation shapes leave out of their own error unions. It is the one that says what happened here: the caller's budget is spent, and no amount of waiting changes that. Every error Converse does declare would say something false — `ThrottlingException` tells an SDK to back off and retry a request that can never succeed, and `ValidationException` blames the request. The refusal keeps the accurate type and the gap is named instead, because a router that lies about WHY it refused costs the caller a retry storm.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'trafficType' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: These two rows are not busbar's bytes — they are GOOGLE'S, captured verbatim off Vertex AI (gemini-2.5-flash, us-central1, 2026-09-07) and committed under crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/tests/proto/golden/vendor/. Every response Vertex returns carries `usageMetadata.trafficType` (the ON_DEMAND vs PROVISIONED billing lane), and the pinned generativelanguage discovery document does not declare it, because that document describes the Gemini API surface and this is the Vertex one. The producer and the schema are both Google's, so there is nothing here for busbar to fix: the recording is what the API sends. Naming it keeps the row honest about the ONE thing it is here to prove — that a field carrying billing-lane meaning reaches busbar undeclared — instead of letting it fail for a reason nobody reads.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'createTime' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: Same recording, same cause as `gemini-vertex-traffic-type`: Vertex stamps every `GenerateContentResponse` with a top-level `createTime` that the pinned generativelanguage schema's response object does not declare. Google's own bytes against Google's own published schema. busbar neither emits nor consumes the field on these rows — it is passing through what the vendor sent — so the disagreement is the schema's to close, not busbar's.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'domain' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: A grounded turn returns `groundingMetadata.groundingChunks[].web` objects carrying `domain` alongside the declared `uri` and `title`. The pinned schema's GroundingChunkWeb declares the other two and not this one, so Google's live grounding response cannot validate against Google's published grounding schema. Recorded rather than fixed for the same reason as its two siblings: these rows exist to measure the VENDOR, and editing the recording to satisfy the schema would destroy the only evidence that the two disagree.
